name: Grafana Cloud Free tier
free_limits: Metrics: 10k active series per month. Logs: 50 GB ingested per month. Traces: 50 GB ingested per month. Profiles: 50 GB per month. Retention: 14 days for metrics, logs, traces, profiles and k6 tests. Visualization: 3 active users per month. IRM (incident response / on-call): 3 active IRM users per month. Synthetic Monitoring: 100k API test executions and 10k browser test executions per month. k6: 500 virtual user hours per month. Frontend Observability: 50k sessions per month. Free stacks are hard-limited on dashboards/folders; 50,000 annotations per stack.
commercial_use: Not restricted in what was read: the pricing page describes Free as 'Perfect for personal projects, exploring new ideas, and early-stage startups' and states no non-commercial clause. No explicit 'commercial use allowed' sentence was found either; the Terms of Service were not opened.
auth_required: Grafana Cloud account; per-stack API tokens / access policies for ingestion.
attribution_or_license_terms: Hosted SaaS under Grafana Cloud terms (not opened). No attribution requirement seen on the pricing page.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Limits read from grafana.com/pricing on 2026-11-13. Logs/traces are 50 GB each with 14-day retention. IRM is included for 3 active users (the page says IRM, it does not name OnCall separately; the OnCall OSS project was archived 2026-03-24 per Grafana docs found in search). The pricing page gives no alert-rule limit for Free and the Alerting docs page read does not state plan availability, so 'alerting is included with no limit' is NOT confirmed. Commercial-use permission is not explicitly stated.

name: Sentry Developer (free) and Team plans
free_limits: Developer (free): 1 user, 5k errors, 50 replays, 5M spans, 1 GB attachments, 5 GB logs, 1 cron monitor, 1 uptime monitor. Team: $29/month ($26/month billed annually), unlimited users, 50k errors, 50 replays, 5M spans, 1 GB attachments, 5 GB logs, 1 cron monitor, 1 uptime monitor. Extra monitors are pay-as-you-go: $0.78 per additional cron monitor and $1.00 per additional uptime monitor per month (docs: 'All Sentry plans include one cron monitor and one uptime monitor').
commercial_use: Allowed (no non-commercial clause on the pricing page read); the binding limit on Developer is 1 user.
auth_required: Sentry account; DSN for SDK ingestion; auth token for API.
attribution_or_license_terms: Hosted SaaS. No attribution requirement seen. Self-hosted Sentry licence was not checked in this pass.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Confirmed on sentry.io/pricing and docs.sentry.io/pricing: only ONE cron monitor and ONE uptime monitor are included on every plan including Team; extras are $0.78 (cron) and $1.00 (uptime) each from the pay-as-you-go budget. Whether a free Developer org can buy extra monitors without upgrading was not confirmed (the docs describe PAYG for Team and Business). Developer is limited to 1 user.

name: Sentry Security Policy Reporting (CSP report-uri / report-to)
free_limits: No separate quota: CSP reports are ingested as events through the project's Security Header endpoint (https://o<orgId>.ingest.sentry.io/api/<project-id>/security/?sentry_key=<public-key>). Inbound-filtered events do not consume quota.
commercial_use: Allowed (part of the Sentry product on every plan).
auth_required: Only the project's public key (sentry_key) in the report URL; no secret.
attribution_or_license_terms: None seen.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: PARTIAL. Confirmed by direct read: Sentry supports capturing CSP violations via report-uri and report-to (docs recommend specifying both). NOT confirmed by direct read: that CSP reports count against the error quota. The quota docs do not mention CSP. A Sentry help-centre article surfaced in search ('Are messages without errors also counted as errors?', sentry.zendesk.com) is summarised as saying event.type csp counts toward the error quota, but the article itself returned a sign-in page, so this rests on the search snippet only. The filtering docs do confirm 'Filtered events do not consume quota'. Treat as: yes, CSP reports spend error quota (5k/month on Developer) unless filtered. Expect-CT / HPKP are not mentioned on the current page. The originally cited URL docs.sentry.io/security-legal-pii/security/security-policy-reporting/ now redirects to a platform chooser.

name: Healthchecks.io
free_limits: Hobbyist: $0/month, monitor 20 jobs, 100 log entries per job (oldest entries removed when full); no SMS/WhatsApp or phone-call credits listed. Supporter: $5/month, same limits as Hobbyist. Business: $20/month ($16/month billed annually), 100 jobs, 1000 log entries per job, 50 SMS and WhatsApp credits, 20 phone call credits, email support. Business Plus: $80/month, 1000 jobs, 500 SMS/WhatsApp credits, 100 phone call credits.
commercial_use: Not restricted on the pricing page (no non-commercial clause). The page asks users not to use multiple accounts to get around the Hobbyist limits ('will be considered abuse'). Terms page not opened.
auth_required: Account for the dashboard/API; each check is pinged at an unguessable UUID URL (or slug + ping key).
attribution_or_license_terms: Open-source server is BSD 3-Clause ('Healthchecks is licensed under the BSD 3-clause license') and can be self-hosted.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: 20 checks and 100 log entries on Hobbyist confirmed; BSD-3 confirmed from the official repo README. Team-member limits are NOT shown on the current pricing page or the projects/teams docs, so the commonly quoted '3 team members' could not be confirmed. Business is free for open-source projects and nonprofits (not applicable here). Self-hosting would be class F3.

name: cron-job.org
free_limits: Free of charge, donation-financed. Request timeout: 30 seconds. Jobs per account: no fixed limit ('fair usage'). Frequency: up to 60 times an hour (every minute). Response read: up to 64 KB, larger output aborts the execution. A job is disabled automatically when it 'subsequently fails more than 25 times'. REST API: 100 requests per day by default ('can be increased upon request'), plus per-endpoint limits (e.g. 5/second for list/get/update/delete, create job 1/second and 5/minute). Sustaining members: 5,000 API requests per day and, per the official blog, a higher execution time limit and higher output limit.
commercial_use: Not addressed directly. Terms: 'You may only create cronjobs for websites which you own' (or have permission for); no uptime or performance guarantees; the operator may shut the service down at any time without notice; and 'The service is not intended for the processing of personal data, sensitive company data, or other confidential data.'
auth_required: Account; API key (Bearer) for the REST API.
attribution_or_license_terms: Service ToS as above. The software is open source on GitHub (pschlan/cron-job.org); its licence was not checked.
suggested_class: F4 existing infrastructure
verification_note: 30 s timeout, 25-failure auto-disable, 64 KB output cap and 100 API requests/day all confirmed on official pages. NOT confirmed: the sustaining-membership price and the exact raised timeout value — the ToS says the member picks an amount from offered options (monthly or yearly) and that membership 'does not result in additional entitlements'; the blog only says 'a higher execution time limit' and points to Settings in the console. cron-job.org/en/members/ returned 404. As the production scheduler: there is NO SLA and the ToS explicitly disclaims guarantees.

name: UptimeRobot Free plan
free_limits: Free: 50 monitors, 5-minute monitoring interval, 1 status page on an UptimeRobot URL. Cheapest paid plan (Solo): about $9/month billed annually ($10 monthly shown), 10 monitors, 60-second interval.
commercial_use: Allowed as of today. Pricing page, Free plan: 'Good for personal and commercial projects. No credit card required!' Terms: 'UptimeRobot is available for any use, including commercial and business use.' A separate Fair Use Policy is referenced but was not opened.
auth_required: Account; API key for the API.
attribution_or_license_terms: Hosted SaaS under UptimeRobot terms (latest changelog entry in the terms: May 26, 2026).
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: SURPRISE: the widely held belief (from the late-2024 terms change) that the free plan is personal / non-commercial only is no longer what the official pages say — both the pricing page and the terms now state commercial use is allowed. Read twice on 2026-11-13. The Fair Use Policy was not read.

name: Better Stack free tier (Uptime + Telemetry)
free_limits: 10 monitors and heartbeats (combined), 1 status page, Slack and e-mail alerts (no phone/SMS, no on-call scheduling). Check frequency: 3 minutes on free plans (30 seconds on paid). Telemetry: 3 GB logs retained for 3 days, 3 GB traces and 3 GB web events retained for 3 days, 30 GB metrics.
commercial_use: Unclear / conditional: the free section of the pricing page is headed 'Free for personal projects'. No explicit non-commercial clause was found on the page, and no explicit permission either; the terms were not opened.
auth_required: Account; API token; source token for log ingestion.
attribution_or_license_terms: Hosted SaaS; no attribution requirement seen.
suggested_class: F5 conditional free
verification_note: Limits confirmed from betterstack.com/pricing and the check-frequency docs. The '10' is monitors AND heartbeats together, not 10 of each. Commercial use for a company is not confirmed — the page positions the free tier for personal projects, so treat as conditional. betterstack.com/docs/uptime/pricing/ returned 404.

name: Cloudflare Turnstile
free_limits: Free: up to 20 widgets, unlimited challenges (traffic or verification requests), 10 hostnames per widget, analytics lookback 7 days maximum. Enterprise: unlimited widgets, up to 200 hostnames per widget, 30 days analytics.
commercial_use: Allowed: the plans page describes Free as suited to small and medium businesses and most production applications; no non-commercial clause.
auth_required: Cloudflare account; site key (public) and secret key for server-side siteverify. The site does not have to be proxied by Cloudflare.
attribution_or_license_terms: Cloudflare terms; no attribution requirement seen.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Confirmed on the official plans page. Unlimited challenges on Free; the limit that matters is 20 widgets and 10 hostnames per widget.

name: Cloudflare DMARC Management
free_limits: 'Available on all plans' (includes Free). No report-volume limit stated on the page read.
commercial_use: Allowed (no restriction stated).
auth_required: Cloudflare account with the domain's DNS on Cloudflare; Cloudflare adds the rua address to the DMARC record.
attribution_or_license_terms: Cloudflare terms.
suggested_class: F5 conditional free
verification_note: Confirmed: 'Available on all plans' and 'available to all Cloudflare customers with Cloudflare DNS'. Condition: the domain must use Cloudflare DNS, so it is only free if the company's zone is (or is moved) on Cloudflare. Whether a partial (CNAME) setup works was not confirmed.

name: Cloudflare Web Analytics
free_limits: Free. Works without changing DNS or using Cloudflare's proxy via a JavaScript beacon snippet. Limit of 10 sites when NOT proxied by Cloudflare (no limit for proxied sites). Rules (proxied sites only): Free 0, Pro 5, Business 20, Enterprise 100.
commercial_use: Allowed (no restriction stated).
auth_required: Cloudflare account; site token embedded in the beacon script.
attribution_or_license_terms: Cloudflare terms; no attribution requirement seen.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Confirmed: 'free, privacy-first analytics for your website without changing your DNS or using Cloudflare's proxy'. Data-retention period and sampling are not stated on the pages read. Note it measures page views/Web Vitals from the browser, so it would run on authenticated internal pages and send page URLs to Cloudflare.

name: Cloudflare Email Routing and Email Workers
free_limits: 'Available on Free and Paid plans'. 200 routing rules per domain; 200 verified destination addresses per account; inbound message size 25 MiB (larger rejected); one destination per rule; reply References capped at 100 entries. Email Workers run on the Workers plan: Free = 100,000 requests/day and 10 ms CPU per invocation, and the limits page warns complex handlers can fail with EXCEEDED_CPU on Workers Free.
commercial_use: Allowed (no restriction stated).
auth_required: Cloudflare account; the domain must use Cloudflare DNS; destination addresses must be verified.
attribution_or_license_terms: Cloudflare terms.
suggested_class: F5 conditional free
verification_note: Confirmed: 'You must be using Cloudflare DNS', and onboarding adds 'MX records to route incoming emails to Cloudflare' — so it replaces the domain's inbound mail path and cannot coexist with an existing mailbox provider's MX on the same name. Subdomain support is NOT confirmed from the pages read (the enable page speaks of the root domain). 25 MiB confirmed.

name: Cloudflare Workers Free plan (Cron Triggers)
free_limits: Workers Free: 100,000 requests/day; CPU time 10 ms per HTTP request and 10 ms per Cron Trigger invocation; memory 128 MB; 50 subrequests per request; 5 Cron Triggers per account; 100 Workers per account; 64 environment variables per Worker. Workers Paid: no request limit, CPU up to 5 min (default 30 s), Cron Trigger CPU 30 s (interval under 1 hour) or 15 min (1 hour or more), 10,000 subrequests per request, 250 Cron Triggers per account.
commercial_use: Allowed (no restriction stated).
auth_required: Cloudflare account; deploy with wrangler/API token.
attribution_or_license_terms: Cloudflare terms.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Confirmed from the official limits table. Free allows only 5 Cron Triggers per ACCOUNT and 10 ms CPU per invocation (wall-clock waiting on a fetch does not count as CPU), 50 subrequests per invocation.

name: Cloudflare R2 free tier
free_limits: Each month, Standard storage only: 10 GB-month storage, 1 million Class A operations, 10 million Class B operations; egress free for all storage classes. Beyond free (Standard): $0.015 per GB-month, $4.50 per million Class A, $0.36 per million Class B. The free tier does not apply to Infrequent Access.
commercial_use: Allowed (no restriction stated).
auth_required: Cloudflare account with R2 enabled; S3-compatible access keys or Workers binding.
attribution_or_license_terms: Cloudflare terms.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Confirmed: 'You can use the following amount of storage and operations each month for free' and 'All included usage is on a monthly basis' — a recurring monthly allowance with no expiry stated (the page does not use the word 'permanent'). Whether enabling R2 requires a payment method on file was not checked. The platform's ~8.7 GB of storage would sit just under the 10 GB allowance, with no headroom.

name: Cloudflare Free plan as reverse proxy / CDN / WAF
free_limits: Free plan: unmetered DDoS protection, Universal SSL, 'Free Managed Ruleset' (the only managed ruleset on Free; Cloudflare Managed Ruleset and OWASP Core Ruleset need Pro or above), simple bot mitigation, 5 custom WAF rules, 1 rate limiting rule (Free: count by IP only, 10 s counting period, 10 s mitigation timeout, match on Path and Verified Bot only). Max upload (request body) size: 100 MB on Free and Pro, 200 MB Business, up to 5 GB Enterprise. Proxy Read Timeout: documented as 125 seconds (error 524); configurable only for Enterprise zones (up to 6,000 s).
commercial_use: Allowed (no restriction stated).
auth_required: Cloudflare account; the domain's nameservers must be Cloudflare's (full setup) to proxy.
attribution_or_license_terms: Cloudflare Self-Serve Subscription Agreement (not opened).
suggested_class: F5 conditional free
verification_note: SURPRISE: the commonly quoted 100-second origin timeout is now documented as 125 seconds — both the connection-limits reference ('Proxy Read Timeout | 125', configurable 'for Enterprise zones') and the Error 524 page ('the default 125 seconds') say so. 100 MB upload cap on Free confirmed (error 413 page). 5 custom rules and 1 rate limiting rule on Free confirmed from the WAF docs. Conditional because the zone's DNS must move to Cloudflare; any request longer than ~125 s or upload over 100 MB would break behind the proxy.

name: ntfy (ntfy.sh)
free_limits: Hosted ntfy.sh free: daily message limit 250; message length up to 4,096 bytes; attachments up to 15 MB each and 100 MB total per visitor, deleted after 3 hours; e-mail notifications 5 per day; burst of 60 requests per visitor; 30 open subscriptions per visitor; scheduled delivery from 10 seconds to 3 days. Paid: Supporter $5/month (2,500 messages/day, 25 MB attachments), Pro $10/month (20,000/day, 250 MB), Business $20/month (50,000/day, 1 GB). Phone calls are paid-plan only.
commercial_use: Not addressed on the site (no restriction stated; 'contact us' for bigger needs). Topics on the free tier are public by name — anyone who knows the topic name can read it — unless a topic is reserved (paid) or the server is self-hosted.
auth_required: None for the free hosted tier (no sign-up); access tokens / reserved topics need an account and a paid plan.
attribution_or_license_terms: Open source, 'dual-licensed under the Apache 2.0 and GPLv2 license'; self-hosting is free.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Limits confirmed from the Limitations section of the official publish docs and the plan table on ntfy.sh. Self-hosting is class F3 (Apache-2.0 / GPLv2). The free hosted tier has no private topics, so nothing identifying an employee should be published to it.

name: Canarytokens (canarytokens.org)
free_limits: Thinkst's help centre lists these token types: Web Bug, DNS, AWS API Key, Azure Login Certificate, Microsoft Word / Excel / macro-enabled, Sensitive Command, Active Directory Login, WireGuard VPN, Cloned Website, Cloned CSS, Azure Entra ID Login, QR Code, Acrobat PDF, Slack API Key (deprecated per the GitHub README), Windows Folder, Custom Exe/Binary, AWS S3 Bucket, Custom Web Image, Office 365 Mail Bug, Slow/Fast Redirect, Google Docs/Sheets, Gmail, Fake App, MySQL Dump. No usage limits for the public site could be read.
commercial_use: Not confirmed from a readable official page. The help article read says tokens are 'completely free' for Canary customers; the free public status of canarytokens.org is long-standing and described in Thinkst blog posts surfaced by search, but its terms could not be opened.
auth_required: Public site: none (an e-mail address or webhook URL to receive alerts).
attribution_or_license_terms: Open-source server on github.com/thinkst/canarytokens ('by Thinkst Applied Research'); the licence file was not read. Self-hosting via Docker is supported.
suggested_class: F1 genuinely free
verification_note: PARTIAL. canarytokens.org/nest renders client-side and returned only a title; docs.canarytokens.org failed to load twice. Confirmed from Thinkst's own help centre and GitHub README: maintained by Thinkst, token list above (AWS API key, DNS, web bug, Word doc and MySQL Dump all present). NOT confirmed: an explicit 'canarytokens.org is free' statement or its terms of use, and a SQL Server token (not in the help-centre list read). Alert content goes to Thinkst's infrastructure and to the e-mail/webhook supplied.

name: Langfuse (Cloud Hobby and self-hosted)
free_limits: Cloud Hobby (free): 50k units per month included, 30 days data access, 2 users, community support via GitHub; regions US, EU or Japan. Core: $29/month, 100k units included then $8 per 100k, 90 days data access, unlimited users. Self-hosted: all product features (tracing, evaluations, prompt management, playground) MIT-licensed with no usage limits.
commercial_use: No restriction stated on the pricing page for Hobby; self-hosted MIT core permits commercial use.
auth_required: Langfuse project public/secret API keys.
attribution_or_license_terms: 'Everything outside the /ee folders is MIT-licensed.' Enterprise Edition code in /ee needs a licence key: examples named are SCIM, audit logging and data retention policies.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Confirmed on langfuse.com/pricing and the open-source docs. EU region is available on Hobby. Hobby is capped at 2 users and 30 days of data. Self-hosting is class F3 and needs its own infrastructure (the self-hosting requirements page was not opened). The docs give only examples of EE-only modules, not a complete list.

name: Supabase pricing and plan limits
free_limits: Pro: from $25/month per organization, includes $10/month compute credits (one Micro instance); 8 GB disk per project then $0.125/GB; 100 GB file storage then $0.0213/GB; 250 GB egress then $0.09/GB plus 250 GB cached egress then $0.03/GB; 100,000 MAU then $0.00325/MAU; Realtime 500 concurrent peak connections then $10 per 1,000, and 5 million messages then $2.50 per million; Edge Functions 2 million invocations then $2 per million; daily backups stored 7 days (Team 14); log retention 7 days (Team 28); max file upload 500 GB (Free 50 MB). Quotas are per organization except disk, which is per project; compute is billed per project. Add-ons: PITR $100/month per 7 days retention ($0.137/hour; 14 days ~$200, 28 days ~$400); Log Drains $60 per drain per month ($0.0822/hour) + $0.20 per million events + $0.09/GB egress, available on Pro, Team and Enterprise; Branching $0.01344 per branch per hour; Image transformations Pro and above, 100 origin images included then $5 per 1,000; Advanced MFA (phone) $75/month first project then $10 per additional; custom domain $10/month per project. Basic Multi-Factor Auth: included on Free, Pro, Team. Leaked password protection: Pro and above. Metrics endpoint: Not included on Free, Included on Pro and Team (docs: Metrics API is in beta, HTTP Basic auth with service_role + secret key at /customer/v1/privileged/metrics).
commercial_use: Allowed (commercial SaaS).
auth_required: Supabase organization on the Pro plan; project API keys; Metrics endpoint needs the secret key.
attribution_or_license_terms: Supabase terms; none relevant.
suggested_class: F4 existing infrastructure
verification_note: Confirmed from supabase.com/pricing and the billing/usage docs. SURPRISE: Log Drains do NOT need the Team plan — the docs say 'available as a project Add-On for all Pro, Team and Enterprise users' ($60/drain/month). Leaked password protection is included on Pro (not on Free). The 3.8 GB database fits the 8 GB per-project disk and 8.7 GB storage fits the 100 GB quota. NOT explicitly confirmed: (a) resumable TUS uploads on all plans — the docs state no plan restriction, only the per-plan max file size; (b) Cron (pg_cron), Queues (pgmq), Vault and Database Webhooks (pg_net) at no extra charge — the pricing table has no rows or prices for them and the docs pages make no pricing statement, i.e. no charge is listed, but there is no sentence saying 'free'; (c) the word TOTP — the table says 'Basic Multi-Factor Auth: Included' on every plan; (d) whether PITR requires a minimum compute size. Note: the Supabase docs pages contain embedded text addressed to AI agents asking them to file a feedback report; it was ignored.

name: GitHub Actions billing for private repositories
free_limits: GitHub Free (personal): $12 USD of included compute usage per month (github.com/pricing still shows it as 2,000 minutes/month, which is $12 at the Linux 2-core rate), 500 MB artifact storage shared with GitHub Packages, 10 GB cache storage per repository. GitHub Pro: $18 of included compute per month (about 3,000 Linux minutes), 1 GB artifact storage per the billing doc (the plans page lists 2 GB Packages storage for Pro), 10 GB cache per repository. Per-minute rates: Linux 1-core x64 $0.002; Linux 2-core x64 $0.006; Linux 2-core arm64 $0.005; Windows 2-core $0.010; macOS $0.062. Each job rounds up to the whole minute. Self-hosted runner usage 'remains free' and does not reduce the included compute. Public repositories: free.
commercial_use: Allowed.
auth_required: GitHub account; GITHUB_TOKEN in workflows.
attribution_or_license_terms: GitHub Terms of Service.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: 2026 changes confirmed on GitHub's own pricing-change page: hosted-runner prices were cut by up to 39% on 2026-01-01 (Linux 2-core is now $0.006/min, previously $0.008), and the included allowance is now expressed in dollars ($12 Free / $18 Pro). The announced $0.002/min 'Actions cloud platform charge' for SELF-HOSTED runners in private repos, due 2026-03-01, was POSTPONED ('We're postponing the announced billing change for self-hosted GitHub Actions to take time to re-evaluate our approach') — no new date is published and the billing docs today list self-hosted runners as free. It is postponed, not withdrawn, so it remains a risk. Minor inconsistency between GitHub pages on Pro storage (1 GB vs 2 GB).

name: GitHub security features for private repositories on the Free plan
free_limits: Included with all plans (private repos too): dependency graph, Dependabot alerts, Dependabot security updates, Dependabot version updates. NOT available on private repos without a paid product: secret scanning and push protection (GitHub Secret Protection, $19 USD per active committer per month) and code scanning / CodeQL, dependency review, Copilot Autofix (GitHub Code Security, $30 USD per active committer per month). Both products can only be bought on GitHub Team or GitHub Enterprise ('must be on a GitHub Team or GitHub Enterprise plan in order to purchase'). For user-owned private repositories the secret-scanning docs list availability only with Enterprise Managed Users. 'Push protection for users' (free, personal) covers pushes to PUBLIC repositories only. Branch protection: available in public repositories on GitHub Free, and in public and private repositories only with GitHub Pro, Team or Enterprise. Rulesets / repository rules: github.com/pricing lists 'Public repositories' for Free.
commercial_use: Allowed.
auth_required: GitHub account / repository admin.
attribution_or_license_terms: GitHub Terms of Service.
suggested_class: F5 conditional free
verification_note: Confirmed across GitHub docs, github.com/pricing and github.com/security/plans. For a PRIVATE repository on a personal GitHub Free account: Dependabot (alerts, security updates, version updates) is free; secret scanning, push protection and CodeQL code scanning are NOT available and cannot even be purchased without moving to a Team organization (then $19 and $30 per active committer per month); branch protection rules and rulesets are NOT enforced on private repos on Free — GitHub Pro ($4/month personal; price not re-read today) is the cheapest plan that enforces them. This matches the repo's own note that branch protection answers 403 on the free plan. Uploading SARIF from a third-party scanner also needs Code Security on a private repo ('If you want to use code scanning on private repositories, you need a GitHub Code Security license').

name: Railway pricing and platform limits
free_limits: Hobby: $5/month including $5 of usage (does not accumulate), up to 48 vCPU / 48 GB RAM per service, 6 replicas, 5 GB volume storage, 2 custom domains, 7-day log retention, 3 members per project. Pro: $20/month per workspace including $20 of usage, up to 1,000 vCPU / 1 TB RAM, 42 replicas, 1 TB volumes, 20 custom domains, 30-day logs, unlimited seats. Free: $0 with $1/month credit, 1 vCPU / 0.5 GB. Usage rates (all plans): RAM $0.00000386 per GB-second (about $10 per GB per month); CPU $0.00000772 per vCPU-second (about $20 per vCPU per month); network egress $0.05 per GB; volumes about $0.15 per GB per month. Regions: us-west2, us-east4-eqdc4a, europe-west4-drams3a (EU West Metal, Amsterdam), asia-southeast1-eqsg3a. Cron: runs at least 5 minutes apart, UTC, a run is skipped if the previous execution is still running. HTTP edge: requests can run up to 15 minutes if data keeps transferring, otherwise closed after 5 minutes with no data transferred; request bodies must finish uploading within 5 minutes; idle HTTP/1.1 keep-alive closed after 60 seconds; 32 KB combined header size; 10,000 concurrent connections; about 11,000 RPS per domain; WebSockets exempt from duration limits.
commercial_use: Allowed (commercial PaaS).
auth_required: Railway account / workspace; project tokens for CLI and API.
attribution_or_license_terms: Railway terms; none relevant.
suggested_class: F4 existing infrastructure
verification_note: Fees, credits, rates, regions list and edge limits confirmed from railway.com/pricing and docs.railway.com. SURPRISE: the documented edge limit is 5 minutes with no data transferred (15 minutes maximum while data flows), not a short fixed timeout. NOT confirmed from official pages: whether cron-scheduled services and multiple environments are available on Hobby (neither the cron nor the environments docs state any plan restriction — only Environment RBAC is Enterprise), and whether Hobby can deploy to europe-west4 / use multi-region replicas (the regions page lists no plan restriction; older community posts conflict). No maximum request body size is documented.

name: Google reCAPTCHA
free_limits: Essentials: free up to 10,000 assessments per calendar month, counted per ORGANIZATION (not per site key). Above that, without billing: 'Requests return a Resource Exhausted (429) quota error' until the quota resets on the first day of the next calendar month. Premium (billing instrument required): 0–10,000 free; 10,001–100,000 assessments per month is a flat $8; above 100,000 is $1 per 1,000 assessments ($0.001 each). Enterprise: volume commitment at $1 per 1,000.
commercial_use: Allowed.
auth_required: Google Cloud project; site key plus API key / service account for assessments.
attribution_or_license_terms: Google Cloud terms; reCAPTCHA branding/notice requirements were not re-read.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Confirmed on Google Cloud docs (cloud.google.com/recaptcha redirects to docs.cloud.google.com). The tiers are named Essentials / Premium / Enterprise (there is no 'Standard'). Exceeding the free quota without billing makes assessment calls fail with 429 for the rest of the month — a login gated on reCAPTCHA must fail open or fall back.

name: OpenAI API pricing
free_limits: No free allowance for model usage is listed: text models are priced per 1M tokens. The only free items on the pricing page are the omni-moderation-latest model ('Free'), search content tokens for some web-search previews, and 1 GB of file-search storage. The rate-limits page lists a usage tier NAMED 'Free' (qualification: user in an allowed geography; $100/month usage limit) below 'Build' ($5 in total credit purchases) — a tier label and spending cap, not a grant of free tokens as far as the page states.
commercial_use: Allowed (paid API under OpenAI business terms).
auth_required: API key (secret), billing set up on the organization.
attribution_or_license_terms: OpenAI Services Agreement / usage policies (not opened).
suggested_class: EXCLUDED (trial/credits/paid)
verification_note: PARTIAL. openai.com/api/pricing returned HTTP 403; platform.openai.com/docs/pricing redirects to developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, which was read: pricing is per token with no permanent free tier described for model usage. NOT confirmed by an explicit official sentence: (a) 'there is no free tier' — the pages simply list none, and the 'Free' usage tier on the rate-limits page was not explained further; (b) that GET /v1/models is not billed — no official page read states this (it consumes no tokens and no per-request price is listed for it). Excluded as a 'free AI' option either way.

name: Google Gemini API free tier
free_limits: A free tier exists for a subset of models (Flash / Flash-Lite class and some others; the top models are paid only), with per-model rate limits not extracted here. Free tier: 'Content used to improve our products' = Yes. Paid tier: 'Used to improve our products' = No.
commercial_use: Restricted for this use: on Unpaid Services Google uses submitted content and responses 'to provide, improve, and develop' its products and machine-learning technologies; human reviewers 'may read, annotate, and process your API input and output'; and the terms say 'Do not submit sensitive, confidential, or personal information to the Unpaid Services.' The no-training treatment for unpaid usage applies only to users in the EEA, UK and Switzerland — Egypt is not covered.
auth_required: Google AI Studio API key.
attribution_or_license_terms: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service.
suggested_class: F5 conditional free
verification_note: Confirmed on Google's pricing and terms pages (ai.google.dev now redirects to aistudio.google.com/docs). Egypt IS in the list of available regions for the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Conclusion for the audit: the free tier is available in Egypt but must NOT be used for employee, HR, payroll or customer data — prompts are used for product improvement and may be read by human reviewers. Only the paid tier gives no-training terms.

name: Upstash QStash free tier
free_limits: Free: 1,000 messages per day (a soft limit — persistent overage leads to contact and possibly 429 errors, not a bill), max message size 1 MB, max delay 7 days, max HTTP response duration 15 minutes, 10 active schedules, 10 queues, queue parallelism 2, max parallelism 10, DLQ retention 3 days, logs retention 3 days. Retries: 3 by default with exponential backoff (each delay capped at 1 day); each retry counts as an additional message. Pay-as-you-go: $1 per 100K messages.
commercial_use: Allowed (no restriction stated).
auth_required: Upstash account; QSTASH_TOKEN to publish; signing keys to verify deliveries.
attribution_or_license_terms: Upstash terms; none relevant.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Confirmed from the official pricing table and retry docs. SURPRISE: the free allowance is 1,000 messages/day (older figures of 500/day are out of date) and retries are billed as messages. A maximum retry count per plan is not listed on the current pricing page, so the per-plan retry cap is NOT confirmed (default is 3).

name: MDN HTTP Observatory
free_limits: Free. v2 API: POST https://observatory-api.mdn.mozilla.net/api/v2/scan?host=<hostname> returns a concise JSON result. 'A site can only be scanned and a new result returned every 60 seconds.' The v1 endpoint was shut down on October 31, 2024.
commercial_use: Not addressed; no API-specific terms on the page (only Mozilla's general website terms link).
auth_required: None.
attribution_or_license_terms: No API terms stated. The scanner is open source (mdn/mdn-http-observatory); its licence was not read.
suggested_class: F1 genuinely free
verification_note: Confirmed the v2 endpoint and the 60-second per-site rescan rule from MDN's own FAQ. No explicit API rate limit or terms of use are published, so automated use should be light (for example one scan per deploy or per day). It only scans publicly reachable hosts and tests response headers, not authenticated pages.

name: Have I Been Pwned — Pwned Passwords range API
free_limits: Free: 'The Pwned Passwords API is freely accessible without the need for a subscription and API key.' 'There is no rate limit on the Pwned Passwords API.' k-anonymity range search sends only the first 5 characters of the SHA-1 (or NTLM) hash.
commercial_use: Allowed in effect: 'there is no licencing or attribution requirements on the Pwned Passwords API' (attribution welcome). The page does not use the words 'commercial use'.
auth_required: None (a User-Agent header is expected on HIBP APIs generally).
attribution_or_license_terms: No licensing or attribution requirement for Pwned Passwords; the CC BY 4.0 licence applies to the breach and paste APIs, not this one.
suggested_class: F1 genuinely free
verification_note: Confirmed on the official API v3 page. Note the overlap: Supabase's built-in leaked password protection (Pro and above) uses the same data set, so a direct integration is only needed for passwords handled outside Supabase Auth.

name: Checkly Hobby plan
free_limits: Hobby (free): 10 uptime monitors (2-minute maximum frequency, 6 locations), 10,000 API check runs per month, 1,000 browser / Playwright check runs per month, 1 user, up to 3 locations per check, raw results kept 7 days and aggregated metrics 30 days, alerts by email, Slack and webhooks (no SMS/phone). Hard cap: checks stop once the monthly amounts are used. Starter: $24/month — 50 uptime monitors, 1-minute frequency, 25,000 API runs, 3,000 browser runs, 3 users, 100 SMS alerts.
commercial_use: Not explicitly restricted; the plan is described as 'Perfect for personal projects and learning'. No non-commercial clause on the pricing page; terms not opened.
auth_required: Checkly account; API key for the CLI / monitoring-as-code.
attribution_or_license_terms: Hosted SaaS; none seen.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Confirmed on checklyhq.com/pricing. Hobby is a single-user plan with a hard cap (checks stop, no overage bill). 1,000 browser runs/month is roughly one synthetic login every 45 minutes; 10,000 API runs/month is roughly one check every 5 minutes for a single endpoint. Commercial use for a company is not confirmed either way.
